name: The existence of solutions
text:
If the equation $A\xvec = \bvec$ is inconsistent, what can we say about the pivot positions of the augmented matrix $\left[\begin{array}{r|r} A \amp \bvec \end{array}\right]$?

We know there must be a pivot position in the rightmost column of the augmented matrix.

We know there must be a pivot position in the rightmost column of the augmented matrix.

Consider the matrix $A$ $$ A = \left[ \begin{array}{rrr} 1 \amp 0 \amp -2 \\ -2 \amp 2 \amp 2 \\ 1 \amp 1 \amp -3 \end{array}\right] $$ . If $\bvec=\threevec{2}{2}{5}$, is the equation $A\xvec = \bvec$ consistent? If so, find a solution.

$\xvec=\threevec{2}{3}{0}+x_3\threevec{2}{1}{1}$

We construct the augmented matrix $$ \left[\begin{array}{rrr|r} 1 \amp 0 \amp -2 \amp 2 \\ -2 \amp 2 \amp 2 \amp 2 \\ 1 \amp 1 \amp -3 \amp 5 \end{array}\right] \sim \left[\begin{array}{rrr|r} 1 \amp 0 \amp -2 \amp 2 \\ 0 \amp 1 \amp -1 \amp 3 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \end{array}\right]\text{,} $$ which shows that the system is consistent. The solution space is described parametrically as $$ \xvec=\threevec{2}{3}{0}+x_3\threevec{2}{1}{1} $$ .

If $\bvec=\threevec{2}{2}{6}$, is the equation $A\xvec = \bvec$ consistent? If so, find a solution.

The equation $A\xvec=\bvec$ is inconsistent.

Now the augmented matrix is $$ \left[\begin{array}{rrr|r} 1 \amp 0 \amp -2 \amp 2 \\ -2 \amp 2 \amp 2 \amp 2 \\ 1 \amp 1 \amp -3 \amp 6 \end{array}\right] \sim \left[\begin{array}{rrr|r} 1 \amp 0 \amp -2 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 1 \amp -1 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \amp 1 \end{array}\right] $$ showing that the equation $A\xvec=\bvec$ is inconsistent.

Identify the pivot positions of $A$.

There are two pivot positions.

There are two pivot positions in $A$, as shown. $$ \left[\begin{array}{rrr} {\mathbf 1} \amp 0 \amp -2 \\ -2 \amp {\mathbf 2} \amp 2 \\ 1 \amp 1 \amp -3 \\ \end{array}\right] \sim \left[\begin{array}{rrr} {\mathbf 1} \amp 0 \amp -2 \\ 0 \amp {\mathbf 1} \amp -1 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ \end{array}\right]\text{.} $$

For our two choices of the vector $\bvec$, one equation $A\xvec = \bvec$ has a solution and the other does not. What feature of the pivot positions of the matrix $A$ tells us to expect this?

There is a row of $A$ without a pivot position.

Since there is a row of $A$ that does not have a pivot position, it is possible to augment $A$ by a vector $\bvec$ so that we obtain a pivot position in the rightmost column of the augmented matrix. In this case, we have an inconsistent system.
